It initializes region-constraint storage, calls `free_region_relations::create` to compute universal-region relations and normalized signature types, constructs a `TypeChecker` with `TypeChecker::new`, then invokes `TypeChecker::check_user_type_annotations`, `TypeVerifier::new`, `TypeVerifier::visit_body`, `TypeChecker::typeck_mir`, `TypeChecker::equate_inputs_and_outputs`, `TypeChecker::check_signature_annotation`, `liveness::generate`, and `translate_outlives_facts` before finalizing opaque-type/member constraints and returning the accumulated `MirTypeckResults`.

Creates a `TypeChecker` with `TypeChecker::new`, runs a defensive `TypeVerifier` over the MIR by constructing it with `TypeVerifier::new` and calling `visit_body`, then, if verification reported no errors, performs the main MIR type-checking pass via `typeck_mir`; finally it invokes the supplied callback `extra` with the checker.

Exports collected outlives constraints into Polonius subset facts when fact generation is enabled. It calls `Locations::from_location` on each constraint to decide whether to emit a single location fact or facts for all points, then extends `subset_base` accordingly.
Reports broken MIR as a delayed compiler bug to avoid premature hard failures for known predicate-checking situations; it forwards the message to `span_delayed_bug`.
Tracks the most recent non-dummy span seen during MIR traversal so later verifier diagnostics can point at a useful source location.
Verifies each visited place by calling `TypeVerifier::sanitize_place`.

Checks constants for structural and typing validity. It calls `super_constant` to recurse, `TypeVerifier::sanitize_type` to validate the constant type, records liveness for free regions, uses `TypeChecker::relate_type_and_user_type` when a user type annotation is present, and for unevaluated/promoted constants may call `TypeChecker::eq_types`, `TypeVerifier::sanitize_promoted`, `TypeChecker::ascribe_user_type`, `TypeChecker::normalize`, `TypeChecker::check_static_ptr`, `TypeChecker::normalize_and_prove_instantiated_predicates`, and `TypeChecker::prove_predicates` to validate promoted bodies, statics, and callable/predicate requirements.
Recurses through an rvalue with `super_rvalue`, computes its MIR type, and calls `TypeVerifier::sanitize_type` to ensure the inferred rvalue type is valid.

Checks each local declaration. It calls `super_local_decl`, validates the declared type with `TypeVerifier::sanitize_type`, and for user type annotations calls `TypeChecker::relate_type_and_user_type` against the adjusted binding type.
Verifies the body-level return type by calling `TypeVerifier::sanitize_type`, then traverses the rest of the MIR with `super_body`.
Constructs a `TypeVerifier` from an existing `TypeChecker`, storing the promoted bodies and initializing the last span from the current body span.
Returns the MIR body currently being verified.
Returns the `TyCtxt` from the underlying type-checking context.
Rejects obviously invalid MIR types by checking for escaping bound vars or error types; otherwise returns the type unchanged.

Validates a place and computes its resulting `PlaceTy`. It starts from the base local type, calls `TypeVerifier::body` and `TypeVerifier::sanitize_projection` for each projection element, uses `TypeVerifier::tcx` when manufacturing error types, and for copy uses calls `TypeChecker::prove_trait_ref` to require that the final type implements `Copy`.

Type-checks a promoted body in isolation and remaps its generated constraints back onto the parent body at a single use location. It swaps in temporary constraint storage, calls `TypeVerifier::visit_body` and `TypeChecker::typeck_mir` on the promoted MIR, then merges outlives and liveness information into the parent context.

Validates one projection step and computes the projected `PlaceTy`. It uses `TypeVerifier::tcx` and `TypeVerifier::body` for type queries, calls `TypeVerifier::sanitize_type` for field results, `TypeVerifier::field_ty` to resolve field access, `TypeVerifier::get_ambient_variance` to determine variance from the use context, and `TypeChecker::normalize` plus `TypeChecker::relate_types` to enforce subtyping/equality constraints introduced by field and opaque-cast projections.
Creates and returns a generic miscellaneous error type using `TypeVerifier::tcx`.

Resolves the type of a field access for structs, enums, closures, coroutine closures, tuples, and coroutine state. It calls `TypeVerifier::tcx` for layout/type queries and `TypeChecker::normalize` before returning field types that depend on instantiated arguments.

Interns a placeholder region into the MIR type-checking constraint set. It reuses an existing mapped region when present; otherwise it creates a fresh NLL region variable and stores it for later reuse.
Returns the concrete source `Location` for `Locations::Single`, or `None` for `Locations::All`.
Returns the representative span for a location set, using the stored span for `All` or the body source info for `Single`.

Constructs the main MIR `TypeChecker` with the borrowck/typeck inputs and empty error tracking. If the next trait solver is enabled for a non-child body, it also calls `TypeChecker::register_predefined_opaques_for_next_solver`.
Returns the MIR body being checked.
Returns whether unsized locals or unsized function parameters are enabled in the current feature set.

Processes canonical user type annotations attached to the MIR body. It calls `TypeChecker::instantiate_canonical_with_fresh_inference_vars`, then dispatches to either `TypeChecker::check_inline_const` for inline-const `TypeOf` annotations or `TypeChecker::ascribe_user_type` for ordinary annotations.

Converts solver-produced region constraints into MIR borrowck constraints by constructing a `constraint_conversion::ConstraintConversion` and calling its `convert_all` method; it also uses `Locations::span` to supply an error span.
Enforces that `sub` is a subtype of `sup` by calling `TypeChecker::relate_types` with contravariant comparison on the expected/supertype side.
Enforces type equality by calling `TypeChecker::relate_types` with invariant variance.

Walks a user type projection from its annotated base type, normalizes each projected field, and then relates the final projected type to `a` with variance-adjusted subtyping. This method explicitly calls `normalize` while resolving projected fields and then calls `relate_types` on the final type.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context.

Type-checks a MIR statement, chiefly assignments and ascriptions, by selecting an appropriate constraint category, normalizing place/rvalue types, enforcing subtype relationships, checking user-provided type annotations, and validating statement-specific operands or trait obligations. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `normalize`, `sub_types`, `rvalue_user_ty`, `relate_type_and_user_type`, `check_rvalue`, and `check_operand`.

Type-checks MIR terminators such as switches, calls, asserts, yields, and coroutine resumes by checking operands, validating control-flow-specific type requirements, instantiating and normalizing call signatures, and enforcing argument/result compatibility. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `check_operand`, `normalize`, `check_call_dest`, `check_call_inputs`, and `sub_types`.

Validates the destination place of a call terminator by normalizing its type, choosing the right constraint category, checking that the function output type is a subtype of the destination type, and enforcing `Sized` for call destinations when unsized features are enabled. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `normalize`, `sub_types`, and `ensure_place_sized`.

Checks call-argument arity and each argument's type against the callee signature, with extra validation for certain SIMD intrinsics that require a constant argument. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `normalize`, `sub_types`, and also uses `tcx` again to query intrinsic metadata and emit diagnostics.

Verifies that cleanup-block flags are consistent with each block's terminator and all of its successors, rejecting invalid mixes such as `resume` or `terminate` on non-cleanup blocks. This method explicitly calls `assert_iscleanup` and `assert_iscleanup_unwind`.
Checks that a target basic block's `is_cleanup` flag matches the expected cleanup state and reports broken MIR if it does not.

Checks local declarations for size requirements, skipping return pointers and arguments, and enforcing `Sized` on temporaries/locals when unsized features are disabled. This method explicitly calls `unsized_feature_enabled` and `ensure_place_sized`.

Erases regions from a type, tests whether the resulting type is `Sized` in the current parameter environment, and emits the unsized-move diagnostic once per reported error site. This method explicitly calls `tcx`.

Computes the expected type of an aggregate field for ADTs, closures, coroutines, coroutine closures, or arrays, reporting out-of-range field access when needed. This method explicitly calls `tcx` and `normalize` for ADT field types.

Checks constant operands for deferred obligations, and for non-promoted inline consts proves and normalizes the instantiated predicates required by their captured environment. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `prove_closure_bounds`, and `normalize_and_prove_instantiated_predicates`.

Type-checks each MIR rvalue form by validating operands, proving well-formedness or trait obligations, checking coercions and casts, and enforcing operation-specific typing rules. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `check_operand`, `check_aggregate_rvalue`, `prove_predicate`, `prove_trait_ref`, `normalize`, and `eq_types`.
Returns the user type annotation attached to an aggregate rvalue when present, and `None` for all other rvalue kinds.

Checks aggregate construction by first proving aggregate-level predicates, then comparing each operand's normalized type against the expected field type and reporting field-count or subtype mismatches. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `prove_aggregate_predicates`, `aggregate_field_ty`, `normalize`, and `sub_types`.

Adds region constraints for reborrows by optionally exporting Polonius `loan_issued_at` facts, determining whether the borrow is for a closure upvar, and walking projections backwards to relate the new borrow region to referenced base regions. This method does not explicitly call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Builds and proves the predicates required by constructing an aggregate, using item predicates for ADTs, closure-specific propagated bounds for closures/coroutines, and no predicates for arrays/tuples. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `prove_closure_bounds`, and `normalize_and_prove_instantiated_predicates`.

Applies propagated closure borrow-check requirements, equates closure parent arguments with the root type-checking item arguments, and returns the instantiated predicates for the closure or inline const. This method explicitly calls `eq_args` from the current checker and otherwise performs constraint conversion setup and predicate instantiation.

Drives MIR type checking for the whole body by checking every local declaration, every statement, every terminator, and each block's cleanup invariants. This method explicitly calls `check_local`, `check_stmt`, `check_terminator`, and `check_iscleanup`.
Trait hook that converts an implementing location-like value into the `Locations` form used by normalization and constraint generation.
Identity conversion from `Locations` to `Locations`.
Wraps a single `Location` as `Locations::Single`.
Performs opaque-type instantiation obligations under region-constraint scraping, stores the collected region constraints back into the error info, and returns the type-op output.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/mir/tcx.rs::im: Constructs a `PlaceTy` from a plain type by storing the type and clearing any downcast variant information (`variant_index: None`).

Computes the type of a field projected from this place type, selecting the appropriate ADT variant when downcasted or indexing into tuple elements; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Computes the type of a single place projection using default callbacks and an empty param environment; explicitly calls `PlaceTy::projection_ty_core`.

Implements the core typing rules for MIR projection elements, handling deref, indexing, subslicing, downcast, field, and opaque-cast projections while preserving or updating downcast state; explicitly calls `PlaceTy::from_ty` when producing projected place types.

Computes a place type from a local plus projection chain by starting from the local declaration type and folding each projection element over it; explicitly calls `PlaceTy::from_ty` and `PlaceTy::projection_ty`.
Computes this `Place`'s type from local declarations and `TyCtxt`; explicitly calls `Place::ty_from`.
Computes this `PlaceRef`'s type from local declarations and `TyCtxt`; explicitly calls `Place::ty_from`.

Computes the result type of each MIR `Rvalue` form, delegating to operand, place, and operator typing for uses, references, pointer formation, arithmetic, aggregates, and box initialization. Explicitly calls `Operand::ty`, `Place::ty`, `BorrowKind::to_mutbl_lossy`, and `BinOp::ty`.
Classifies rvalue initialization as shallow only for `ShallowInitBox` and deep for all other rvalues; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Returns the type of an operand by reading the referenced place type for `Copy`/`Move` operands or the literal type for constants; explicitly calls `Place::ty`.

Determines the result type of a MIR binary operator, yielding the operand type for arithmetic/bitwise operations, the left-hand type for shifts and pointer offset, and `bool` for comparisons; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Converts MIR borrow kinds into HIR mutability, mapping mutable borrows to `Mut` and shared or shallow borrows to `Not`; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Maps MIR binary operators to their corresponding HIR binary operator kinds, rejecting unchecked and offset-only MIR operators as unreachable; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/generat: Returns the visitor's stored type context for MIR mutation; it does not call any other listed method.
Renames a local by replacing `from` with `to` when the visited local matches; it does not call any other listed method.
Skips rewriting `Return` terminators so the implicit `_0` access is preserved, and otherwise delegates traversal to `super_terminator`.
Returns the visitor's stored type context for deref-based self-argument rewriting; it does not call any other listed method.
Rejects any direct visit to `SELF_ARG`, enforcing that the self argument must be handled through place rewriting instead of local replacement; it does not call any other listed method.

Rewrites any place rooted at `SELF_ARG` to insert a dereference for the by-reference generator argument by calling `replace_base`; otherwise it validates the base local through `visit_local` and checks indexed projections do not mention `SELF_ARG`.
Returns the visitor's stored type context for pin-based self-argument rewriting; it does not call any other listed method.
Rejects any direct visit to `SELF_ARG`, ensuring the pinned self argument is only adjusted through place rewriting; it does not call any other listed method.

Rewrites any place rooted at `SELF_ARG` to project through the `Pin` wrapper's field by calling `replace_base`; otherwise it validates the base local through `visit_local` and checks indexed projections do not mention `SELF_ARG`.
Replaces a place's base local/projection with a new base and appends the original projection suffix to produce the rewritten place; it does not call any other listed method.

Builds the return-state aggregate written to `_0`, choosing the correct `GeneratorState` or `Poll` variant and handling the special zero-field `Poll::Pending` case; it does not call any other listed method.
Constructs a `Place` that accesses a generator field by downcasting `SELF_ARG` to a state variant and projecting the requested field; it does not call any other listed method.
Creates a `SetDiscriminant` statement that writes the generator's current state discriminant onto `SELF_ARG`; it does not call any other listed method.
Allocates a temporary local and returns an assignment statement that reads the discriminant of `SELF_ARG` into that temporary; it does not call any other listed method.
Returns the transform visitor's stored type context; it does not call any other listed method.

Asserts that a visited local is not directly present in the remap table, ensuring remapped locals are handled through place rewriting instead of raw local visitation; it does not call any other listed method.

Rewrites places whose base local was promoted into generator storage by calling `make_field` to build the corresponding generator-field access and then `replace_base` to splice it into the original place.

Transforms blocks containing `return` or `yield` by removing storage statements for remapped locals, packaging the yielded/returned value via `make_state`, remapping resume destinations with `make_field` and `replace_base` when needed, recording suspension metadata, setting the generator discriminant with `set_discr`, rewriting the terminator to `Return`, and finally recursing with `super_basic_block_data`.

Changes the generator self argument from by-value to `&mut` and then rewrites all self accesses to dereference that reference by calling `DerefArgVisitor::visit_body`; it does not call any other listed method from this file.

Wraps the generator self argument type in `Pin` and then rewrites all self accesses to project through the pinned field by calling `PinArgVisitor::visit_body`; it does not call any other listed method from this file.
Creates a replacement local with a new type, swaps it into the original slot, and then renames all references from the old local to the new one by calling `RenameLocalVisitor::visit_body`.

Computes which locals must survive across generator suspension points by running storage, borrow, requires-storage, and liveness dataflow analyses, collecting per-yield live sets and storage liveness, renumbering saved locals with `GeneratorSavedLocals::renumber_bitset`, and computing overlap constraints with `compute_storage_conflicts`.
Iterates over saved locals while pairing each `Local` with its compact `GeneratorSavedLocal` index; it does not call any other listed method.
Converts a `BitSet<Local>` into a `BitSet<GeneratorSavedLocal>` by iterating saved locals through `iter_enumerated` and inserting the compact index for each contained local.
Looks up the compact saved-local index corresponding to a `Local`, returning `None` if the local is not saved; it does not call any other listed method.
Returns the underlying bitset of saved locals by dereferencing the wrapper; it does not call any other listed method.

Builds the pairwise storage-conflict matrix for saved generator locals by analyzing locals that must remain live, visiting reachable MIR with storage requirements, and compressing conflicts into saved-local indices using `GeneratorSavedLocals::iter_enumerated`.

Updates the storage-conflict matrix for a program point by ignoring unreachable blocks, intersecting the live set with saved locals, and marking all simultaneously live eligible locals as conflicting.

Sanity-checks that every non-ignored generator field type in the computed layout is present in the typeck-provided generator witness or upvar set, reporting a bug if MIR contains extra suspended types.

Computes generator layout metadata from liveness information, including saved-local to field mappings, saved field types, per-variant suspended locals, and storage liveness snapshots for suspension points.

Prepends a new entry block that reads the generator discriminant and dispatches to state-specific blocks via `SwitchInt`, then renumbers existing successor targets to account for the inserted block. It explicitly calls `insert_term_block` and `TransformVisitor::get_discr`.

Finds drops of the generator self local in the drop shim body and expands them into detailed drop glue with correct unwind handling. It explicitly calls `elaborate_drop` and finally applies the accumulated MIR patch.

Builds a generator drop shim by cloning the body, creating per-state drop entry cases, dispatching on the discriminant, rewriting generator-drop terminators to returns, adjusting argument and return types, simplifying dead code, and running unwind-abort cleanup passes. It explicitly calls `create_cases`, `insert_switch`, and `make_generator_state_argument_indirect`.
Appends a new basic block containing only the given terminator and returns its block index.
Appends an always-failing assert block carrying the given panic message and returns the new block index.
Determines whether the body can return normally by rejecting uninhabited return types and otherwise checking for any `Return` terminator.
Determines whether the body may unwind by first honoring abort panic strategy and then scanning terminators for any operation kind that can start unwinding.

Transforms the generator body into its resume/poll entry function by adding poisoning-on-unwind logic, creating state dispatch cases, inserting panic cases for invalid resumed states, rewriting entry dispatch, adjusting the self argument form, simplifying CFG, and running cleanup passes. It explicitly calls `can_unwind`, `TransformVisitor::set_discr`, `create_cases`, `insert_panic_block`, `insert_switch`, `make_generator_state_argument_indirect`, and `make_generator_state_argument_pinned`.
Creates the special block used to drop an unresumed generator by first making a return block and then appending a `Drop` of `SELF_ARG` that targets it. It explicitly calls `insert_term_block`.
Selects the suspension-point target block appropriate for the current operation, returning the resume block for `Resume` and the optional drop block for `Drop`.

Creates per-suspension-point entry blocks for resume or drop dispatch, restoring needed `StorageLive`s, reassigning the resume argument on resume paths, and jumping to the original target block. It explicitly calls `Operation::target_block`.

Runs the main generator lowering pass: validates generator MIR, derives generator/state types, rewrites the return local and async resume context, computes liveness and layout, validates witness information, and prepares the transformed body for resume/drop state-machine generation. It explicitly calls `replace_local`, `transform_async_context`, `always_storage_live_locals`, `locals_live_across_suspend_points`, `compute_layout`, `sanitize_witness`, and `can_return`.
Maps a direct, non-indirect place to its saved generator local if one exists, otherwise returning `None`.

Temporarily records the saved local assigned on the left-hand side, runs a callback to inspect the corresponding right-hand side, and then clears the assignment context. It explicitly calls `saved_local_for_direct_place`.

While checking an assignment RHS, verifies that any referenced saved generator local conflicts in storage with the currently assigned saved local, otherwise reports a bug. It explicitly calls `saved_local_for_direct_place`.

Inspects assignment statements for forbidden non-conflicting saved-local aliasing by visiting the RHS under the LHS assignment context, while ignoring all other statement kinds. It explicitly calls `check_assigned_place` and, through the callback, `visit_rvalue`.

Checks terminators that assign into a destination saved local—calls and yields—by visiting their input operands under the destination assignment context, while ignoring non-assigning terminators. It explicitly calls `check_assigned_place` and, through callbacks, `visit_operand`.

ResultsVisitor hook invoked before a statement’s primary effect; it forwards the current dataflow state and location to `apply_state` to record/update storage-conflict information for that point. Calls `apply_state`.

ResultsVisitor hook invoked before a terminator’s primary effect; it delegates to `apply_state` with the current flow state and location so storage-conflict tracking is updated at terminator boundaries. Calls `apply_state`.
Declares that the `StateTransform` MIR pass advances the body to the `MirPhase::GeneratorsLowered` phase after generator lowering is complete.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/match: Iteratively simplifies a candidate’s `match_pairs` to a fixed point, preserving binding order across iterations and splitting the candidate into or-pattern subcandidates when the remaining single pair is an `Or` pattern. This method calls `simplify_match_pair` for each extracted match pair, and calls `create_or_subcandidates` when it detects a top-level or-pattern case.

Builds one fresh `Candidate` per branch of an or-pattern, reusing the original place and guard state, and simplifies each branch before returning the collected subcandidates. This method calls `simplify_candidate` on every newly created subcandidate.

Simplifies a single `MatchPair` according to its pattern kind, recording bindings and type ascriptions on the candidate, expanding structural or irrefutable pattern forms into derived field/subpattern match pairs, and returning unsimplified pairs unchanged when they still require runtime testing. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/mod.r: Builds or reuses the MIR body for a local item. If `def.try_upgrade(tcx)` succeeds, it delegates to `tcx.mir_built`; otherwise it calls `mir_build` to construct MIR, adjusts the source for const-parameter instances with `MirSource::from_instance`, and returns the allocated stolen MIR via `tcx.alloc_steal_mir`.

Main MIR-construction dispatcher for a body owner. It queries HIR/typeck state, forces prerequisite unsafety and abstract-const analyses, identifies the body/return-type span from HIR, then builds an inference context and dispatches to either `construct_fn`, `construct_const`, or `construct_error` depending on the item kind and whether THIR/typeck construction failed.

Computes the closure environment type with late-bound regions liberated for MIR building. It reads the closure type from `tcx.typeck_body(body_id).node_type`, derives the environment type with `tcx.closure_env_ty`, and erases the late-bound region binder with `tcx.erase_late_bound_regions`.
Returns whether this block frame represents a tail-expression context by pattern-matching on `BlockFrame::TailExpr`.
Returns whether this block frame represents a statement context by pattern-matching on `BlockFrame::Statement`.
Checks whether a local variable id is currently tracked in any active match-guard frame by scanning `guard_context` with nested iterator `any` tests.
Maps a THIR local-variable id to the MIR local to use in the current guard mode. It calls `LocalsForNode::local_id` on the entry stored in `self.var_indices`.
Creates an empty `BlockContext` with no active block frames.
Pushes a `BlockFrame` onto the block-context stack.
Pops and returns the most recent `BlockFrame` from the block-context stack.
Finds the nearest enclosing tail-expression frame that is not masked by a statement frame by iterating the block-context stack in reverse, and returns its tail-result metadata if present.
Reports whether the current block context should ignore a tail expression's result, based on the last active frame in the stack.
Constructs a `GuardFrameLocal` that records only the bound local variable id for guard tracking.

Selects the MIR local to use for a binding, choosing between the ordinary local and the guard-specific reference local depending on `ForGuard`, and bugs if a single-local binding is incorrectly requested from within a guard.
Trait method that combines a basic block with an arbitrary value into a `BlockAnd<T>` pair.
Trait method that converts a basic block into a `BlockAnd<()>` pair carrying unit.
Wraps this `BasicBlock` and a supplied value into `BlockAnd<T>`.
Wraps this `BasicBlock` into `BlockAnd<()>` with a unit payload.

Builds MIR for a function or closure body. It collects arguments, creates a `Builder` with `Builder::new`, enters call-site and argument scopes via `builder.in_scope`, enters the return breakable scope with `builder.in_breakable_scope`, lowers parameters and the body by calling `builder.args_and_body`, emits the final return terminator with `builder.cfg.terminate`, finalizes drops with `builder.build_drop_trees`, uses `return_block.unit()` to package the scope result, and completes the MIR with `builder.finish`.

Builds MIR for a constant or static initializer. It creates a `Builder` with `Builder::new`, lowers the THIR expression into the return place by calling `builder.expr_into_dest`, emits a `Return` terminator with `builder.cfg.terminate`, runs `builder.build_drop_trees`, and returns the finished body from `builder.finish`.

Constructs fallback error MIR for items whose earlier compilation stages failed. It computes parameter count from HIR, creates minimal CFG/source-scope/local-decl state, adds parameter locals, terminates the start block as `Unreachable` with `cfg.terminate`, builds the body with `Body::new`, and records a generator yield type when applicable.

Initializes the MIR `Builder` state for a body, computing overflow-check behavior, parameter/typeck/region context, CFG and local tables, and other bookkeeping. It also initializes the CFG start block with `builder.cfg.start_new_block` and creates the outermost source scope by calling `builder.new_source_scope`.
Finalizes MIR construction. It validates that every basic block has a terminator by iterating the CFG, then creates the finished MIR body with `Body::new`.

Allocates MIR locals for function arguments, records argument debug info, prepares closure/generator capture metadata and upvar debug info when needed, schedules capture drops, and lowers argument patterns and the function body into MIR. During argument lowering it calls `self.set_correct_source_scope_for_arg` to adjust lint/source scopes for each argument pattern.

Adjusts the current source scope when an argument pattern belongs to a different lint-level root than its parent scope. If the roots differ, it creates a replacement scope by calling `self.new_source_scope`.
Returns a cached temporary place for unit values, creating it on first use by calling `self.temp` with `tcx.mk_unit()` and then storing the result in `self.unit_temp`.

Converts a parsed literal plus its target type into a MIR `ConstantKind`, handling strings, byte strings, bytes, integers, floats, booleans, and chars, and rejecting mismatched or erroneous literals. For integer literals it uses an internal truncation closure that calls `reveal_all`, `and`, `layout_of`, `map_err`, `bits`, `truncate`, and `from_uint` to size the value to the destination type. For string and byte-string references it calls `kind`, `is_str`/`is_array`, `as_str`, `as_bytes`, `from_bytes_byte_aligned_immutable`, `intern_const_alloc`, `len`, `allocate_bytes`, `from_pointer`, and `into` to build the appropriate allocation-backed constant. It also calls `parse_float` and `ok_or` for floats, `from_bool` for booleans, `from_char` for chars, and finally wraps the result with `Val`.

Relates a `TypeAndMut` pair by first requiring identical mutability, then choosing covariance for shared references and invariance for mutable ones before calling `relate_with_variance` on the pointee type.
Relates two substitution lists invariantly element-by-element and rebuilds them in the current type context; it calls `tcx` and `relate_with_variance`.
Relates two substitution lists using a provided variance per parameter, computing invariant diagnostic info from the instantiated item type when needed; it calls `tcx` and `relate_with_variance`.

Relates function signatures by checking variadicity and arity, relating unsafety and ABI directly, then relating inputs contravariantly and the output normally while remapping sort and mutability errors to argument-indexed forms; it calls `tcx`, `relate`, and `relate_with_variance`.
Relates bound constness by requiring exact equality and otherwise reporting `ConstnessMismatch`; it does not call other covered methods.
Relates unsafety flags by requiring exact equality and otherwise reporting `UnsafetyMismatch`; it does not call other covered methods.
Relates ABIs by requiring exact equality and otherwise reporting `AbiMismatch`; it does not call other covered methods.
Relates projection types only when they name the same associated item, then relates their substitutions and rebuilds the projection; it calls `relate`.
Relates existential projections only when they share the same associated item, then invariantly relates both the projected term and substitutions; it calls `relate_with_variance`.
Relates trait references only when they point to the same trait definition, then relates their substitutions; it calls `relate_substs`.
Relates existential trait references only when they point to the same trait definition, then relates their substitutions; it calls `relate_substs`.
Relates two generator-witness type lists positionally after asserting equal length, rebuilding the witness from the related element types; it calls `tcx` and `relate`.

Relates impl subjects only when both are trait impls or both are inherent impls, delegating to trait-ref or type relation accordingly and treating mixed shapes as impossible; it calls `impl<'tcx> Relate<'tcx> for ty::TraitRef<'tcx>::relate` and `impl<'tcx> Relate<'tcx> for Ty<'tcx>::relate`.
For `Ty<'tcx>`, the `Relate` implementation is just a thin forwarder to the relation’s type hook; it calls `tys`.

Structural fallback for relating concrete `Ty<'tcx>` shapes: it rejects inference and bound types, propagates error types, handles primitive/param/placeholder equality, and rebuilds matching composite types such as ADTs, trait objects, generators, closures, pointers, references, arrays, and others by delegating to relation hooks with the correct variance. It calls `tcx`, `with_cause`, `relate_item_substs`, `relate_with_variance`, `relate`, and `relate_type_and_mut`.

Structural fallback for relating constants: it checks type compatibility, eagerly evaluates both sides, compares compatible const forms, recursively relates substs for matching unevaluated constants, and rebuilds the result or reports `ConstMismatch`. It calls `tag`, `tcx`, `param_env`, `check_const_value_eq`, and `relate_with_variance`.

Compares evaluated constant values for structural equality across scalars, function pointers, slices, references, and by-reference aggregates; for aggregate constants it destructures both sides and recursively relates each field constant. It calls `tcx`, `param_env`, and `consts`.

Relates two existential predicate lists by collecting, sorting, and deduplicating both sides, rejecting different list sizes with `TypeError::ExistentialMismatch` via `expected_found`. It then pairwise matches predicate kinds and recursively calls `relation.relate` for corresponding `Trait` and `Projection` entries, keeps equal `AutoTrait` entries unchanged, and finally rebuilds the list with `tcx.mk_poly_existential_predicates`.
Relates two `ty::ClosureSubsts` by calling `relate_substs` on their underlying substitution lists and returning a new `ClosureSubsts` with the related substs.
Relates two `ty::GeneratorSubsts` by calling `relate_substs` on their underlying substitution lists and returning a new `GeneratorSubsts` with the related substs.
Relates two substitution lists directly by calling `relate_substs`.
Delegates region relation to the relation context by calling `relation.regions`.
Delegates const relation to the relation context by calling `relation.consts`.
Delegates binder relation to the relation context by calling `relation.binders`.

Relates two generic arguments only when their variants match: it calls `relation.relate` for paired lifetimes, types, or consts and converts the related result back into a `GenericArg`. Mixed variants are treated as impossible and trigger `bug!`.
Relates impl polarity by requiring exact equality; on mismatch it returns `TypeError::PolarityMismatch` constructed with `expected_found`.
Relates a trait predicate field-by-field, calling `relation.relate` on `trait_ref`, `constness`, and `polarity`, then rebuilding the predicate from the related components.

Relates two terms only when both are the same variant: it calls `relation.relate` for `Ty` pairs and for `Const` pairs, converts the result back into a term, and returns `TypeError::Mismatch` for mixed variants.
Relates a projection predicate field-by-field by calling `relation.relate` on `projection_ty` and `term`, then rebuilding the predicate.
Builds an `ExpectedFound<T>` by calling `ExpectedFound::new` with the relation's `a_is_expected()` polarity and the two provided values.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/thir/cx/exp: Stack-safe entry point for lowering one HIR expression to THIR. It calls `mirror_expr_inner` inside `ensure_sufficient_stack` to avoid deep-recursion stack overflow.
Lowers a slice of HIR expressions to THIR `ExprId`s by iterating over the slice and calling `mirror_expr_inner` for each element.

Performs the core lowering of one HIR expression: computes its temporary lifetime, builds the initial THIR node with `make_mirror_unadjusted`, applies every typeck adjustment by repeatedly calling `apply_adjustment`, then wraps the result in explicit scope and optional destruction-scope THIR nodes before storing it.

Converts a single type-checker `Adjustment` into the corresponding THIR form, handling pointer casts, `NeverToAny`, builtin and overloaded deref, and borrow/reference adjustments while refining spans for diagnostics. For overloaded deref cases it calls `overloaded_place`, and it also uses `to_borrow_kind` to translate mutability into THIR borrow kinds.

Builds the unadjusted THIR `Expr` for a HIR expression by pattern-matching over expression forms and lowering each case before later adjustment handling. Depending on the expression kind, it calls other lowering helpers including `mirror_exprs`, `mirror_expr`, `method_callee`, `mirror_expr_cast`, `convert_path_expr`, `convert_var`, `convert_arm`, `field_refs`, `capture_upvar`, `overloaded_operator`, and `overloaded_place`.

Finds the canonical user-provided type/substitution information associated with a resolved callable, constant, or constructor path. For unit constructors and `Self` constructors it calls `user_substs_applied_to_ty_of_hir_id`; otherwise it reads the typeck user-provided type entry directly.

Constructs the THIR callee expression for a method or overloaded operator as a zero-sized function-definition literal. When no explicit overloaded callee is supplied, it calls `user_substs_applied_to_res` to preserve user-written substitutions.

Lowers a match arm into THIR by converting its pattern, optional guard, body, lint level, and scope. It calls `pattern_from_hir` for the arm pattern and `mirror_expr` for guard expressions and the arm body.

Lowers path expressions into the appropriate THIR form for functions, constructors, const params, constants, statics, and local variables. It calls `user_substs_applied_to_res` for callable/constant paths and `convert_var` for local or captured variable references.
Converts a variable HIR id into either a THIR `UpvarRef` or `VarRef` by checking whether the variable is mentioned as an upvar in the current closure body.
Builds a THIR call expression for an overloaded operator invocation. It calls `method_callee` to obtain the operator method callee, then packages the provided arguments into `ExprKind::Call`.

Builds the THIR for overloaded place expressions such as overloaded deref or indexing by calling the operator method and then wrapping the returned reference in a dereference. It calls `method_callee` to construct the overloaded method callee.

Reconstructs a captured closure place as a THIR expression by starting from the captured upvar base and replaying deref/field projections. It calls `convert_var` to create the base upvar expression before layering projections on top.

Lowers one closure capture into THIR, either reusing the captured place directly for by-value captures or wrapping it in a borrow for by-reference captures. It calls `convert_captured_hir_place` to build the underlying captured-place expression.
Lowers struct/union field initializers into THIR `FieldExpr` entries. It calls `mirror_expr` for each field value expression while computing the THIR field index.
Trait method contract for converting a mutability/auto-borrow description into a THIR `BorrowKind`.
Maps `AutoBorrowMutability` into the corresponding THIR `BorrowKind`, preserving whether two-phase borrowing is allowed for mutable autoborrows.
Maps HIR mutability into the corresponding THIR `BorrowKind`, producing mutable borrows without two-phase borrowing or shared borrows for immutable cases.
Translates a HIR binary operator kind into the matching THIR/MIR `BinOp`, rejecting unsupported operators with a bug.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/thir/patter: Entry point for lowering a HIR pattern into a THIR pattern: it builds a `PatCtxt`, then calls `lower_pattern` to perform the actual recursive lowering and return the final boxed pattern.

Lowers a pattern with type-checker adjustments applied. It first calls `lower_pattern_unadjusted` to build the base THIR pattern, then wraps that result in `PatKind::Deref` layers according to `pat_adjustments` in reverse order.

Builds a THIR range pattern, validates endpoint ordering, and canonicalizes singleton inclusive finite ranges into constant patterns. It calls `lower_pattern_range_endpoint` for both bounds and, on invalid ranges, calls `error_on_literal_overflow` on each endpoint before emitting the range-ordering error.

Performs the main recursive lowering for a HIR pattern before implicit deref adjustments are re-applied. Depending on the pattern kind, it calls `lower_lit`, `lower_pattern_range`, `lower_path`, `lower_pattern`, `slice_or_array_pattern`, `lower_tuple_subpats`, `lower_opt_pattern`, and `lower_variant_or_leaf` to lower substructure and specialized forms.
Lowers tuple field patterns into indexed `FieldPat` entries, accounting for `..` gaps. It calls `lower_pattern` on each tuple subpattern.
Lowers a slice of HIR patterns into boxed THIR patterns. It calls `lower_pattern` for each element.
Lowers an optional HIR subpattern when present. It calls `lower_pattern` on the contained pattern and returns `None` unchanged otherwise.

Constructs the THIR form for slice and fixed-length array patterns after lowering their parts. It calls `lower_patterns` for the prefix and suffix and `lower_opt_pattern` for the middle slice binding, then chooses `PatKind::Slice` or `PatKind::Array` based on the matched type.

Lowers a resolved path-like pattern into either a variant pattern, a leaf pattern, or an error pattern depending on the resolved `Res` and matched type, while also attaching any user-provided type arguments. It does not call other methods from this file.

Lowers a path pattern by distinguishing enum/struct-like paths from constant paths. For non-const paths it calls `lower_variant_or_leaf`; for const and associated-const paths it resolves and evaluates the constant, then converts the result into a pattern with `const_to_pat` or returns an error pattern if evaluation fails.

Lowers an inline `const` used in a pattern, preferring a fast literal path when possible and otherwise falling back to const evaluation. It calls `const_to_pat` both for directly converted literals and for successfully evaluated constant results, producing an inline-constant pattern wrapper or an error pattern on failure.

Lowers a literal-like pattern expression into a THIR pattern. It dispatches to `lower_path` for path expressions, to `lower_inline_const` for inline const blocks, and otherwise converts the literal to a constant and calls `const_to_pat`.
Trait helper accessor that returns the `TyCtxt` stored in `PatCtxt`. It does not call other methods from this file.
Trait helper accessor that returns the stored type-check results. It does not call other methods from this file.

Constructs a new `PatCtxt` from the type context, parameter environment, and type-check results, initializing error storage and disabling lint checks by default. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Enables lint-check behavior on the existing `PatCtxt` and returns the same context for chaining. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Lowers a HIR range endpoint expression into a `PatKind`, extracting and returning any `AscribeUserType` wrapper as a separate ascription. This method calls `lower_lit`.

Normalizes optional lower and upper range pattern endpoints into concrete constant bounds, filling missing numeric bounds with the type’s min or max value when possible. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Provides the default folding entry point for foldable pattern data by delegating to the type’s structural folding implementation. This method calls `super_fold_with`.
Declares the structural folding hook that implementors must provide to recursively fold their contents with a `PatternFolder`. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Defines the default way a folder processes a full `Pat` by delegating to the pattern’s structural folding logic. This method calls `super_fold_with`.
Defines the default way a folder processes a `PatKind` by delegating to the kind’s structural folding logic. This method calls `super_fold_with`.
Structurally folds the boxed value and rebuilds a new `Box` containing the folded result. This method calls `fold_with`.
Structurally folds each element of the vector and collects the folded elements into a new vector. This method calls `fold_with`.
Structurally folds the contained value when the option is `Some`, preserving `None` unchanged. This method calls `fold_with`.

Implements structural folding for leaf-like types by returning a clone unchanged, since they contain no nested foldable pattern structure. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Structurally folds both the field identifier and the nested field pattern, then rebuilds the `FieldPat`. This method calls `fold_with`.
Makes `Pat` use the folder’s pattern-level customization point instead of the default structural path directly. This method calls `fold_pattern`.
Structurally folds a pattern’s type, span, and kind, then reconstructs the `Pat`. This method calls `fold_with`.
Makes `PatKind` use the folder’s kind-level customization point instead of directly performing structural recursion. This method calls `fold_pattern_kind`.

Performs structural recursion over each `PatKind` variant, folding nested subpatterns and foldable fields while leaving leaf variants unchanged, then reconstructs the corresponding pattern kind. This method calls `fold_with`.

Compares two pattern constants under a given type and parameter environment, preferring evaluated-bit comparisons for numeric and float types, handling string slices specially, and falling back to equality-only comparison when precise ordering is unavailable. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/check/pat.rs::: Builds the `ObligationCause` used for pattern-type errors from the top-level pattern context and span. It calls `cause` after packaging the pattern metadata into a `Pattern` cause code.

Checks pattern type equality and returns a deferred diagnostic if the expected and actual types differ. It calls `pattern_cause` to create the pattern-specific obligation cause, then calls `demand_eqtype_with_origin`.
Enforces exact type equality for a pattern and immediately emits any resulting error. It calls `demand_eqtype_pat_diag` and, when that returns a diagnostic, calls `emit` on it.
Top-level entry point for pattern checking that creates the initial `TopInfo` and starts recursion with the initial binding mode. It calls `check_pat`.

Main recursive dispatcher for all HIR pattern kinds: it resolves path patterns, computes reference-adjustment/default-binding behavior, delegates to specialized pattern checkers, recurses through `or` patterns, and records the resulting type for the pattern node. It calls `resolve_ty_and_res_fully_qualified_call`, `calc_adjust_mode`, `calc_default_binding_mode`, `check_pat_lit`, `check_pat_range`, `check_pat_ident`, `check_pat_tuple_struct`, `check_pat_path`, `check_pat_struct`, `check_pat` recursively for `Or` alternatives, `check_pat_tuple`, `check_pat_box`, `check_pat_ref`, `check_pat_slice`, and finally `write_ty`.

Applies the chosen adjustment policy to the expected type and current default binding mode. For `Peel`, it calls `peel_off_references`; otherwise it either preserves the inputs or resets to `INITIAL_BM`.

Determines whether pattern checking should preserve references, reset binding-mode state, or peel reference layers based on the pattern form and, for literals/paths, the resolved expression or item kind. It calls `check_expr` and `resolve_vars_if_possible` when inspecting literal patterns.

Strips as many outer reference layers as possible from the expected type, updates the default binding mode to match Rust's match-ergonomics rules, and stores the implicit deref adjustments for the pattern. It calls `resolve_vars_with_obligations` and records adjustments through `pat_adjustments_mut().insert(...)` when any references were peeled.

Type-checks a literal pattern, including the special byte-string-to-slice behavior, and verifies that the literal type is a subtype-compatible match for the expected type. It calls `node_ty`, `structurally_resolved_type`, `pattern_cause`, and `demand_suptype_with_origin`, and emits the resulting diagnostic with `emit_unless` if needed.

Type-checks a range pattern by checking both endpoints, rejecting non-numeric/non-`char` endpoints early, unifying each endpoint with the expected type, and producing an error type on failure. It calls `check_expr` for each endpoint, `emit_err_pat_range` for invalid endpoint categories, `demand_eqtype_pat_diag` to compare endpoint and expected types, `endpoint_has_type` to enrich diagnostics, and `structurally_resolved_type` when finishing the unified-type validation.
Adds a diagnostic label describing an endpoint's type when that type is not already erroneous. It calls `span_label` on the diagnostic.

Builds and emits the dedicated error for range patterns whose endpoints are not numeric or `char`, annotating one or both endpoint spans and optionally adding a teaching note. It calls `resolve_vars_if_possible`, `endpoint_has_type`, `get_code`, `note`, and `emit`.

Type-checks a binding pattern by determining and recording its binding mode, computing the binding's expected type, enforcing equality with the local's declared type, checking alternative-arm consistency, and recursively checking any subpattern. It calls `local_ty`, `new_ref_ty` for `ref` bindings, `demand_eqtype_pat`, `check_binding_alt_eq_ty`, and `check_pat` for an attached subpattern.

Verifies that the same binding name appearing in multiple alternatives has a consistent type and emits a tailored diagnostic if not. It calls `local_ty`, `demand_eqtype_pat_diag`, and `resolve_vars_with_obligations`, then labels the original binding site and emits the error.

Adds borrow-related fix-it suggestions for explicit reference patterns when the inner pattern is a simple binding, tailoring the suggestion to parameter versus nested-pattern contexts. It calls HIR parent lookups and `span_to_snippet`, then emits suggestions with `span_suggestion`.

Checks whether an explicitly dereferencing pattern can legally dereference the expected type, with a special diagnostic for trait-object cases reduced to binding patterns. It calls `shallow_resolve`, `builtin_deref`, `ty_to_string`, and, on error, `span_label`, `get_code`, `note`, and `emit`.

Type-checks a struct pattern by resolving the struct path, checking its type against the expected type, and then validating and recursively checking the field subpatterns. It calls `check_struct_path`, `check_pat` on each field with an error type when path resolution fails, `demand_eqtype_pat`, and `check_struct_pat_fields`.

Type-checks a constant/self-constructor path pattern after validating that the resolved item kind is allowed in patterns, then instantiates the path type and checks it against the expected type. It calls `set_tainted_by_errors` on resolution failure, `report_unexpected_variant_res` for disallowed constructors/functions, `instantiate_value_path`, `pattern_cause`, `demand_suptype_with_origin`, and `emit_bad_pat_path` for mismatch diagnostics.

Detects when a referenced constant is itself a range literal and, if so, adds a suggestion to inline that range into the match pattern. It calls local-HIR lookup helpers, `hir::is_range_literal`, `span_to_snippet`, and `span_suggestion_verbose`.

Emits the detailed diagnostic for a path pattern that resolved to an existing item instead of a fresh binding, including notes for struct-field contexts and special suggestions for range-like constants. It calls HIR `res_span`, labels spans, and may call `maybe_suggest_range_literal` before finally emitting the diagnostic.

Type-checks tuple-struct and tuple-variant patterns by resolving and instantiating the path, rejecting non-constructor resolutions with custom diagnostics, validating constructor arity/type information, and recursively checking subpatterns. It calls `check_pat` in its recovery path, `resolve_ty_and_res_fully_qualified_call`, `set_tainted_by_errors`, `instantiate_value_path`, `demand_eqtype_pat_diag`, `check_stability`, `field_ty`, and `e0023` for wrong-field-count diagnostics.

Constructs the `E0023` diagnostic for tuple-struct/tuple-variant patterns with the wrong number of subpatterns, highlighting both use and definition sites and suggesting fixes such as inserting missing tuple parentheses. It gathers field and pattern spans and emits a multipart or direct suggestion before calling `emit`.

Type-checks tuple patterns by synthesizing tuple element inference variables, equating the whole tuple pattern with the expected type, and recursively checking each element with its corresponding element type; on mismatch it rechecks elements against error types to suppress follow-on errors. It calls `structurally_resolved_type`, `next_ty_var`, `demand_eqtype_pat_diag`, `check_pat`, and constructs the final tuple type.

Validates and type-checks the fields inside a struct pattern by indexing variant fields, rejecting duplicates and unknown names, recording field indices, checking field stability and field types, recursively checking each field subpattern, and enforcing exhaustiveness/non-exhaustive and visibility rules. It calls `error_field_already_bound`, `write_field_index`, `check_stability`, `field_ty`, `check_pat`, `error_inexistent_fields`, and `error_foreign_non_exhaustive_spat`.

Builds a diagnostic for tuple variants incorrectly written with struct-pattern shorthand field syntax like numeric field names, and suggests the corresponding tuple-pattern form. It calls `get_suggested_tuple_struct_pattern` to build the replacement text.
Emits the error for matching a foreign `#[non_exhaustive]` struct without `..`, and suggests adding `..` at the end of the field list. It calls `span_suggestion_verbose` and `emit`.
Emits the duplicate-field error for struct patterns that bind the same field more than once. It labels both occurrences and calls `emit`.

Builds the diagnostic for struct-pattern fields that do not exist on the matched variant, adding typo suggestions and, when possible, coercion-based or tuple-variant-oriented guidance. It calls `find_best_match_for_name`, `field_ty`, and may add notes based on `teach`, but returns the diagnostic for the caller to emit.

Builds a diagnostic for tuple variants written using struct-pattern syntax and suggests a tuple-pattern replacement, choosing a precise or fallback suggestion based on arity. It calls `get_suggested_tuple_struct_pattern` when it can form an exact replacement.

Formats the replacement text for converting a mistaken struct-style tuple-variant pattern into tuple syntax by reusing each field pattern snippet when possible and substituting `_` for numeric pseudo-field names. It uses source snippets or pretty-printing to assemble the final comma-separated pattern string.

Builds and returns a diagnostic for struct patterns that must include `..` because some fields are inaccessible, choosing an insertion suggestion after the last written field or after the struct path when no fields were written. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Emits the `non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns` lint for omitted struct fields by first formatting the omitted field names and then building a lint message with labels, help, and a note about the matched type. It calls `joined_uncovered_patterns` from the Methods List.

Formats a short human-readable description of omitted field identifiers, either listing one name, listing a few names, or truncating with an `and N more` suffix. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Builds and returns E0027 for struct patterns that omit required fields, labels the missing fields, and, when possible, adds a machine-applicable suggestion to insert the missing fields and optionally `..` for inaccessible ones. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Type-checks a `box` pattern by verifying the expected type is dereferenceable, creating an inferred boxed inner type, equating it with the expected type, and then recursively checking the inner subpattern. It calls `check_pat` from the Methods List.

Type-checks a `&` or `&mut` pattern by resolving the expected type, reusing the expected reference type when possible or constructing a fresh one otherwise, reporting mismatches with diagnostics and borrow-pattern suggestions, and then recursively checking the inner subpattern with updated parent context. It calls `new_ref_ty` and `check_pat` from the Methods List.

Constructs a fresh reference type for a pattern by creating a new pattern region variable and combining it with the given mutability and pointee type. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Type-checks slice and array patterns by structurally resolving the expected type, determining the element type and optional middle-slice type, reporting an error for non-array/slice inputs, and recursively checking each `before`, middle `slice`, and `after` subpattern. It calls `check_array_pat_len`, `error_expected_array_or_slice`, and `check_pat` from the Methods List.

Validates how an array pattern's fixed and rest parts relate to the array length, returning the inferred middle-slice type and possibly a refined array type, or emitting length-related errors when the pattern cannot match. It calls `error_scrutinee_inconsistent_length`, `error_scrutinee_with_rest_inconsistent_length`, and `error_scrutinee_unfixed_length` from the Methods List.
Emits E0527 when a fixed-length array pattern requires a different number of elements than the array type provides. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Emits E0528 when an array pattern with a rest pattern still requires more elements than the matched array type contains. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Emits E0730 when matching an array pattern with a rest element against an array whose length is not known at type-check time. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Emits E0529 when a slice pattern is used against a non-array/slice type, with extra guidance for references, autoderef cases, `Option`/`Result` values that may need `as_deref`, and values that may need slicing syntax. It calls `is_slice_or_array_or_vector` from the Methods List.

Recursively checks whether a type is a `Vec`, array, slice, or reference to one, returning both the boolean result and the innermost relevant type for diagnostics. It calls itself recursively from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/check/upvar.rs: Entry point for upvar analysis on a body: it creates `InferBorrowKindVisitor` and calls `visit_body` to walk the body and analyze nested closures, then checks that deferred call resolutions are empty.
Builds the user-facing Rust 2021 migration warning text, choosing whether to mention drop order, auto-trait changes, or both based on `auto_traits.is_empty()` and `drop_order`.

Visits expressions while descending into nested bodies. For closure expressions it calls `visit_body` on the closure body and then `analyze_closure`; for const blocks it calls `visit_body`; afterward it continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_expr`.

Main closure-capture analysis pipeline: reads the closure or generator type, runs `ExprUseVisitor` to collect capture facts, logs them with `log_capture_analysis_first_pass`, refines them with `process_collected_capture_information`, stores minimal captures with `compute_min_captures`, optionally runs `perform_2229_migration_anaysis`, computes final captured types with `final_upvar_tys`, synthesizes coarse captures when precise capture is disabled by calling `place_for_root_variable` and `init_capture_kind_for_place`, and finally records/logs results with `log_closure_min_capture_info`.
Computes the final tuple of captured upvar types for a closure by iterating flattened minimal captures and calling `apply_capture_kind_on_capture_ty` for each captured place.

Post-processes first-pass capture facts to infer closure kind and origin, while normalizing each capture. It calls `restrict_capture_precision`, `truncate_capture_for_optimization`, then adjusts captures for closure mode with `adjust_for_move_closure` or `adjust_for_non_move_closure`, and finally applies `restrict_precision_for_drop_types` before collecting the processed captures.

Reduces processed captures to a minimal per-root-variable set, merging ancestor/descendant places and combining capture requirements. It calls `determine_capture_mutability` for new roots, uses `determine_place_ancestry_relation` to compare places, and updates merged entries with `truncate_place_to_len_and_update_capture_kind` and `determine_capture_info`.

Runs Rust 2021 closure-capture migration diagnostics for one closure. It calls `compute_2229_migrations` to determine needed migrations and reasons, uses `migration_suggestion_for_2229` to build a suggestion, and formats the lint using `MigrationWarningReason::migration_message` plus `drop_location_span` for drop-order notes.
Constructs and normalizes a `MigrationWarningReason` from collected auto-trait and drop-order causes by extending the reason set and sorting it for deterministic diagnostics.

Checks whether precise capture changes alter which auto traits a captured variable contributes to. It combines captures with `determine_capture_info` when needed and derives the effective captured type with `apply_capture_kind_on_capture_ty`, then compares auto-trait implementation results to produce per-capture migration reasons.

Detects whether precise by-value captures can change drop order for a variable with significant drop. For partially moved captures it calls `has_significant_drop_outside_of_captures` to decide whether uncaptured parts still need drop and returns migration notes describing the responsible captures.

Aggregates Rust 2021 migration requirements across all mentioned upvars in a closure. For each variable it calls `compute_2229_migrations_for_trait` and `compute_2229_migrations_for_drop`, merges their per-capture diagnostics, and summarizes the overall reason with `compute_2229_migrations_reasons`.

Recursively decides whether parts of a value outside the closure’s by-move captures still contain significant drop behavior, accounting for complete capture, explicit `Drop` impls, and structural decomposition of ADTs, references, pointers, and tuples.

Chooses the initial capture mode for a root place from the closure capture clause: move closures default to `ByValue` unless the place is accessed through references, otherwise it yields an immutable `ByRef` capture.
Builds a `Place` representing an uncaptured root upvar by creating its `UpvarId`, looking up the variable type with `node_ty`, and returning a place with no projections.
Returns whether capture-analysis diagnostics should be emitted for a closure by checking for the `rustc_capture_analysis` attribute.

Emits debugging diagnostics for first-pass capture facts when logging is enabled. It first calls `should_log_capture_analysis`, then formats each capture with `construct_capture_info_string` and reports it.

Emits debugging diagnostics for the final minimal captures of a closure when logging is enabled.
